title: itembank evidence event
description: One line of _evidence/evidence.jsonl, built by evidence.response_event() / evidence.hint_event() and written by evidence.append_event() alone. Version 2 (Phase 6) adds the closed hint event shape and an integer-or-null response hint_tier (D-15/D-16) while keeping version-1 reads compatible. The response_event branch is the response shape: additionalProperties is false and every key is required, so a consumer can tell 'not captured' from 'this field did not exist in that era'. mark, retraction, day_tick, term_lookup, key_review, model_interaction and mark_proposal events get real bodies from the matching evidence constructors (described in $defs below) and are accepted by a permissive catch-all branch so a log mixing event types validates as a whole.

event_id.description: A uuid4 hex identifying this event

event_type.description: This branch is the response shape only. 'hint' has its own closed branch (Phase 6); mark/retraction/day_tick/term_lookup/key_review/model_interaction/mark_proposal events fall to the catch-all branch.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC to millisecond precision, matching evidence.utc_now()

item_id.description: The opaque [ID:] identity field when assigned (plan 01-04); empty string on an item that has never had id-assign run against it

item_ref.description: The Qn-derived positional id, always present regardless of whether item_id has been assigned

bank.description: The bank file's basename only, never an absolute path (T-1-06) -- a consumer should not expect a resolvable path here

subject.description: The text before the first ':' in a namespaced objective (evidence.subject_of); empty string on an unnamespaced or empty objective

mode.description: Captured live on every surface; this is what makes a drill-mode correct distinguishable from an exam-mode correct. 'legacy' is written only by itembank migrate (plan 01-11), for an imported record whose source (an attempt markdown file, which never recorded a mode) carries no mode of its own.

attempt_number.description: One more than the count of prior response events for this session and this item

answer.description: The learner's raw response, shaped per item type -- a string, an array, or an object

canonical.description: evidence.idempotency_canon()'s output: runtime.canonical_response() when it returns one, or 'short:' + sha256 of the whitespace-collapsed, lowercased answer text when canonical_response() returns null (a short item has no canonical form of its own). This is the same value fed into dedupe_key, so the two can never compare against different things (D-17, plan 01-07); never null.

score.description: true, false, or null for a constructed response not yet marked -- not-yet-marked and marked-wrong are different states

response_time_ms.description: Captured live; milliseconds between the item being served and the response being submitted; null only when the session carries no served_ts.

confidence.description: Captured live where the surface offers it (submit --confidence); null when the learner did not say, which is different from low confidence.

error_category.description: Reserved, always null in this phase. No error taxonomy exists; it depends on the tutoring work in Phase 8. A guessed category would be recorded as fact and read as fact by later trend work, so it is recorded as unknown instead.

hint_tier.description: The highest tier actually shown at submission time (D-15, Phase 6). Null means no tier was shown -- a different fact from 'tier 0 was shown', which records 0; conflating them is unrecoverable once written. Version-1 events wrote null always.

selection_mode.description: The selection composition that served this item (plan 07-04); `mode` names the feedback policy that governed what was shown. Null when the event predates phase 7.

review_state.description: 'n/a' for an auto-scored item, 'pending' for a constructed response awaiting a marker, 'marked' once a mark event lands.

dedupe_key.description: A sha256 hex digest identifying one attempt at one item in one session

source_ref.description: Null for a live-path response event. For an event imported by itembank migrate (plan 01-11), an object naming where the record came from and how its item_id was resolved -- never a guess left unstated (D-14).

kind.description: Which legacy store this record came from

path.description: The legacy source file's basename only, never a full path

ref.description: The reference identifying this record within its source file -- an attempt file's item heading number, or a session file's array-index-plus-item_id

resolution.description: 'unresolved' by default (item_id is empty string); 'position' only when --resolve-by-position matched this record's positional reference against today's bank by current item number

mark_event.description: The mark event's real shape (plan 01-09, D-12): a first-class, timestamped fact about a response event, appended alongside it and never a mutation of it -- the response event's own score stays null forever, and review_state is computed at read time from evidence.marks_by_event(), never written back.

retraction_event.description: D-10's compensating-append undo, given a real body by evidence.retraction_event() in plan 01-07 (retracts/reason/actor/dedupe_key alongside the standard envelope).

day_tick_event.description: The day_tick event's real shape (plan 01-10): a lane marked done on a date, appended by the day POST route rather than mutating daily_log.md in place.

term_lookup.description: The term_lookup event's real shape (plan 03.1-02, D-19): a learner looked up a lesson term's definition; it is not a response and carries no score key.

key_review.description: The key_review event's real shape (plan 03.1-03, D-19): a learner asked to add a [!KEY] card to review; it is not a response and carries no score key. Phase 10 replays these events into scheduler state.

model_interaction_event.description: The model_interaction event's real shape (plan 08-03, D-12/D-15/D-16): one attempted model generation -- a hint or a rubric review -- logged with backend/profile, operation, timing, request/output fingerprints, outcome, gate result, and permitted tier. A drop/unavailable outcome stores descriptors only and never the dropped candidate's text (pass_payload is null unless outcome is pass). Structurally no score key: an interaction is a fact about the model, never accepted evidence about the learner.

gate_reason.description: Plan 08-01's machine-readable reason code for a drop/unavailable (e.g. gate.ambiguous), or null when the interaction passed.

backend_class.description: Whether the provider was hosted or local (D-17), so later audits can distinguish exposure.

pass_payload.description: The gated, learner-facing content, present only when outcome is pass; null for a drop or unavailable (D-16).

parent_interaction_id.description: The interaction id this retry re-runs, or null for a first attempt (D-12).

mark_proposal_event.description: The mark_proposal event's real shape (plan 08-03, D-13/D-14/D-23): a pending per-point pass|fail|uncertain suggestion for the short-answer response event named by response_event_id, produced by the interaction named by interaction_id. It structurally carries no score key and no verdict field, so it can never be mistaken for the settled mark that only a human's mark_event(marker='human', proposal_ref=...) creates. An empty points array is valid and reads as pending/unknown.

response_event_id.description: The event_id of the genuine short-answer response this proposal reviews.

interaction_id.description: The model interaction that produced this suggestion (D-13).

points.description: One suggestion per rubric point. Empty is valid and reads back as pending/unknown, never a default pass (D-22).

rationale.description: Bounded at 240 characters by the builder (the in-repo validator has no maxLength).
